assumptions: The failing division was attributed to the account-page rendering path in the newly enabled feature on the basis of log correlation with the flag ramp; no one read the code or reproduced the crash during the incident, so the exact line and the input condition that makes the divisor zero are unconfirmed.

The competing explanation (an unrecorded deploy introducing the defect, with the flag change merely coincidental) was dismissed because the change channel showed no deploy in the preceding 24 hours. This assumes the change channel records all deploys.

The low-level UpstreamTimeout errors on the account page (payment authorization timeouts) were present throughout the hour before the flag change and are treated as unrelated pre-existing background noise, not part of this incident. They were not investigated.
Recovery is inferred from the service returning to baseline behaviour after the flag was set off; no separate verification of the account page was recorded beyond that.

The share of account-page requests that hit the faulty path was inferred from per-minute error-rate warnings, not from a breakdown of affected accounts or users, so who was affected (all users vs. accounts with a particular spend history) is not established.
input.executive_summary: On 12 September 2026, customers loading their account page on the online shop began seeing failures. The failures started at about 15:02 UTC, when a new spending-summary feature was switched on for a small slice of traffic and then for all traffic a minute later; the new code crashed on a portion of account page loads. Automated monitoring raised an alert at 15:07:58 UTC, investigated, and identified the newly enabled feature as the cause. The feature was switched back off, and the service returned to its normal behaviour; the alert closed at 15:09:09 UTC. Only the account page was affected, and only for as long as the feature was on — customers who reloaded after the switch-off saw a working page. No data was lost or corrupted, and no code deployment or rollback was required. The underlying defect is still present in the code and is currently contained only by the feature being disabled; it must be fixed and covered by a test before the feature is enabled again.
input.root_cause: Enabling the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop (ramped to 10 of 200 evaluations at 15:02 UTC, fully on by 15:03) activated a previously dormant code path in account-page rendering that performs an unguarded division, raising ZeroDivisionError for the subset of requests whose input made the divisor zero. Error onset tracked the flag ramp minute for minute, and turning the flag off at 15:09 returned the service to its prior baseline.
